title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: Compositional data (CoDa) vectors parts carry relative information : parts sum constant, increasing one part necessarily decreases others, standard statistics raw parts misleading. usual remedy work log-ratios parts, live ordinary Euclidean space. running example 24-hour movement behaviour composition used ProPASS consortium: minutes per day vigorous physical activity (vpa), moderate physical activity (mpa), light physical activity (lipa), sleep (sleep) sedentary behaviour (sb), sum 1440. dsCodaClient lets run workflow across DataSHIELD servers without seeing individual records. Every server needs dsBase, dsCoda (regression step) dsTidyverse installed.

title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: Parts columns data frame; one row per participant. Parts must strictly positive. Zeros allowed composition, replace first (see ). Every server must hold parts column names.

what: A DSLite session with three studies
title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: simulate three studies. handful participants zero minutes vigorous activity, happens real accelerometer data. real servers build logindata Opal Armadillo credentials; everything datashield.login() identical.
code: library(DSI) library(DSLite) library(dsBaseClient) library(dsTidyverseClient) library(dsCodaClient)  set.seed(1) make_study <- function(n, zeros) {   x <- data.frame(     id = seq_len(n),     vpa = rgamma(n, 2, 1) * 10 + 1,     mpa = rgamma(n, 3, 1) * 30 + 1,     lipa = rgamma(n, 4, 1) * 60 + 1,     sleep = rnorm(n, 480, 40),     sb = rnorm(n, 600, 60),     bmi = rnorm(n, 26, 4)   )   x$vpa[sample(n, zeros)] <- 0   x } study1 <- make_study(120, 8) study2 <- make_study(150, 10) study3 <- make_study(90, 6)  dslite.server <- newDSLiteServer(   tables = list(study1 = study1, study2 = study2, study3 = study3),   config = DSLite::defaultDSConfiguration(include = c("dsBase", "dsCoda", "dsTidyverse")) )  builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder() for (s in c("study1", "study2", "study3")) {   builder$append(server = s, url = "dslite.server", table = s, driver = "DSLiteDriver") } conns <- DSI::datashield.login(builder$build(), assign = TRUE, symbol = "D")

what: 1. Replace zeros before closing the composition
title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: ds.lrEM() runs log-ratio EM algorithm zCompositions::lrEM() server. replaces values flagged label imputed values detection limits dl, given scale data (minutes ). raw parts, ds.acomp(). Note z.delete = TRUE (default) drops rows whose parts zero, check dimensions still match D combining objects.
code: parts <- c("vpa", "mpa", "lipa", "sleep", "sb")  ds.select(df.name = "D", tidy_expr = list(vpa, mpa, lipa, sleep, sb),           newobj = "D_parts", datasources = conns)  ds.lrEM(X = "D_parts", label = 0, dl = rep(1, length(parts)),         objectname = "D_imp", datasources = conns) ds.dim("D_imp", datasources = conns) #> $`dimensions of D_imp in study1` #> [1] 120   5 #>  #> $`dimensions of D_imp in study2` #> [1] 150   5 #>  #> $`dimensions of D_imp in study3` #> [1] 90  5 #>  #> $`dimensions of D_imp in combined studies` #> [1] 360   5

title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: ds.acomp() creates compositions::acomp object server. Parts can given name index; total = 1 rescales row proportions.
code: ds.acomp(X = "D_imp", parts = parts, objectname = "comp", datasources = conns) ds.class("comp", datasources = conns) #> $study1 #> [1] "acomp" #>  #> $study2 #> [1] "acomp" #>  #> $study3 #> [1] "acomp"

title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: ILR transform maps D-part composition D - 1 orthonormal coordinates. build_sequential_ilr_V() builds basis sequential binary partition: coordinate 1 contrasts vpa parts, coordinate 2 contrasts mpa parts , . Reorder parts want different first contrast. ds.ilr() sends basis servers stores coordinates. V = NULL default basis compositions::ilrBase() used instead.
code: V <- build_sequential_ilr_V(length(parts), parts) round(V, 3) #>         ilr1   ilr2   ilr3   ilr4 #> vpa    0.894  0.000  0.000  0.000 #> mpa   -0.224  0.866  0.000  0.000 #> lipa  -0.224 -0.289  0.816  0.000 #> sleep -0.224 -0.289 -0.408  0.707 #> sb    -0.224 -0.289 -0.408 -0.707 ds.ilr(X = "comp", V = V, objectname = "ilr_sbp", datasources = conns)

title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: ds.meanComp() computes mean ILR coordinate across servers dsBaseClient::ds.mean(type = "combine") inverts transform client. result pooled geometric-mean composition, compositional analogue arithmetic mean.
code: mean_comp <- ds.meanComp("comp", datasources = conns) round(mean_comp, 4) #>    vpa    mpa   lipa  sleep     sb  #> 0.0098 0.0561 0.1532 0.3474 0.4336 round(mean_comp * 1440)  # back to minutes per day #>   vpa   mpa  lipa sleep    sb  #>    14    81   221   500   624

title: Compositional data analysis with dsCodaClient
text: coordinates stored compositions::rmult matrix, ds.glm() address column. Convert tibble first; columns come named V1 V4, V1 first column V (ilr1), V2 ilr2, . Server-side messages glm.fit convergence warnings single-step IRLS iterations hidden chunk; normal DataSHIELD GLM algorithm stay server real connection. coefficient ilr_tbl$V1 change BMI per unit increase first coordinate, .e. vpa relative behaviours.
code: ds.as_tibble("ilr_sbp", newobj = "ilr_tbl", datasources = conns) ds.colnames("ilr_tbl", datasources = conns)$study1 #> [1] "V1" "V2" "V3" "V4"  fit <- ds.glm(   formula = "D$bmi ~ ilr_tbl$V1 + ilr_tbl$V2 + ilr_tbl$V3 + ilr_tbl$V4",   family = "gaussian", datasources = conns ) round(fit$coefficients, 3) #>             Estimate Std. Error z-value p-value low0.95CI high0.95CI #> (Intercept)   26.313      1.130  23.284   0.000    24.098     28.528 #> ilr_tbl$V1    -0.004      0.226  -0.019   0.985    -0.448      0.439 #> ilr_tbl$V2     0.090      0.418   0.214   0.830    -0.730      0.909 #> ilr_tbl$V3    -0.536      0.515  -1.040   0.298    -1.546      0.474 #> ilr_tbl$V4     3.231      2.247   1.438   0.151    -1.174      7.635 DSI::datashield.logout(conns)

title: Build sequential ILR basis matrix (sequential binary partition) — build_sequential_ilr_V
text: numeric `D x (D - 1)` matrix whose columns form orthonormal basis   ILR coordinates sequential SBP. Row names taken   `part_names` provided; column names `ilr1`, ..., `ilr(D-1)`.

title: Build sequential ILR basis matrix (sequential binary partition) — build_sequential_ilr_V
text: resulting `V` can supplied `compositions::ilr(x, V = V)`   perform isometric log-ratio (ILR) transformation based sequential   binary partition. Column `j` contrasts part `j` remaining parts `j+1..D`,   appropriate normalizing constants ensure orthonormality.

title: Creates a server-side Aitchison composition object for compositional data analysis — ds.acomp
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{    # connecting to the DataSHIELD servers    require('DSI')   require('DSOpal')   require('dsBaseClient')   require('dsCodaClient')    builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()   builder$append(server = "study1",                   url = "http://192.168.56.100:8080/",                   user = "administrator", password = "datashield_test&",                   table = "COMPOSITIONAL.DATA1", driver = "OpalDriver")   builder$append(server = "study2",                   url = "http://192.168.56.100:8080/",                   user = "administrator", password = "datashield_test&",                   table = "COMPOSITIONAL.DATA2", driver = "OpalDriver")   logindata <- builder$build()      connections <- DSI::datashield.login(logins = logindata, assign = TRUE, symbol = "D")       # Create a server-side Aitchison composition object   # Using all columns of the dataset   dsCodaClient::ds.acomp(X = 'D',                           objectname = 'comp_object',                          datasources = connections)    # Using specific columns   dsCodaClient::ds.acomp(X = 'D',                           parts = c(1, 2, 3),                          total = 100,                          objectname = 'comp_object_subset',                          datasources = connections)    # Using column names   dsCodaClient::ds.acomp(X = 'D',                           parts = c('component1', 'component2', 'component3'),                          objectname = 'comp_object_named',                          datasources = connections)      # clear the DataSHIELD R sessions and logout   datashield.logout(connections) } # }

title: Creates a server-side log-ratio EM algorithm object for compositional data imputation — ds.lrEM
text: X character string specifying name server-side dataset matrix containing compositional data. label unique label (numeric character) used denote unobserved values X. Default NULL. dl numeric vector matrix detection limits/thresholds. must given scale X. Default NULL. rob logical value. FALSE provides maximum-likelihood estimates model parameters, TRUE provides robust parameter estimates. Default FALSE. ini.cov initial estimation either log-ratio covariance matrix (ML estimation) unobserved data (robust estimation). can based either complete observations ("complete.obs") multiplicative simple replacement ("multRepl"). Default "complete.obs". frac ini.cov="multRepl", fraction parameter initial multiplicative simple replacement left-censored data expressed proportions. Default 0.65. tolerance convergence criterion EM algorithm. Default 0.0001. max.iter maximum number iterations EM algorithm. Default 50. rlm.maxit rob=TRUE, maximum number iterations embedded robust regression estimation. Default 150. imp.missing TRUE unobserved data identified label treated missing data. Default FALSE. suppress.print suppress printed feedback. Default FALSE. closure closure value used add residual part needed ini.cov="multRepl" used. Default NULL. z.warning threshold proportion modified zeros per part warning issued. Default 0.8. z.delete logical value indicating whether rows containing zeros deleted prior imputation. Default TRUE. objectname character string specifying name new server-side object store log-ratio EM imputation result. datasources list DSConnection-class objects obtained login. datasources argument specified, default set connections used: see datashield.connections_default.

title: Creates a server-side log-ratio EM algorithm object for compositional data imputation — ds.lrEM
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{    # connecting to the DataSHIELD servers    require('DSI')   require('DSOpal')   require('dsBaseClient')   require('dsCodaClient')    builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()   builder$append(server = "study1",                   url = "http://192.168.56.100:8080/",                   user = "administrator", password = "datashield_test&",                   table = "COMPOSITIONAL.DATA1", driver = "OpalDriver")   builder$append(server = "study2",                   url = "http://192.168.56.100:8080/",                   user = "administrator", password = "datashield_test&",                   table = "COMPOSITIONAL.DATA2", driver = "OpalDriver")   logindata <- builder$build()      connections <- DSI::datashield.login(logins = logindata, assign = TRUE, symbol = "D")       # Create a server-side log-ratio EM imputation   # Using default parameters   dsCodaClient::ds.lrEM(X = 'D',                          label = 0,                         objectname = 'imputed_data',                         datasources = connections)    # Using specific detection limits   dsCodaClient::ds.lrEM(X = 'D',                          label = 0,                         dl = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),                         rob = FALSE,                         tolerance = 0.001,                         objectname = 'imputed_data_custom',                         datasources = connections)    # Using robust estimation   dsCodaClient::ds.lrEM(X = 'D',                          label = 0,                         dl = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1),                         rob = TRUE,                         ini.cov = "multRepl",                         frac = 0.5,                         objectname = 'robust_imputed_data',                         datasources = connections)      # clear the DataSHIELD R sessions and logout   datashield.logout(connections) } # }
